subject: Model consultation: multivariate GP / multivariate forecasting

messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: Model consultation: multivariate GP / multivariate forecasting
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on the following problem and my initial through is that a multi-variate GP can be the solution.

My question is 2 folded:
1. does it make sense to solve it this with the multi_gp distribution from the manual?
2. if so, is there somethere I can find examples/documentation of this?

Problem:

We have N image recognition robots and a training set of K images.

Each image has a human with a set of known real-value biometric attributes (vector of length J)

vector[J] y[K]

Each of these robots were presented with each of the image and would output its forecasts of the entire set of biometric of the human in the image:

matrix [N, J] x[K]

Now, we presented a new image (k+1) to each robot and received a new set of forecasts:

matrix [N, J] x_tilde;

I would like to construct a posterior for y_tilde.

Some considerations:
- for each k, y[k, *] should be correlated as they represents attributes of the same human being - drawn from mult-normal dist
- the quality of the algorithm of each robot should have an impact for all guess made by the robot (x[*, *, n])
- forecasts from robots can be somewhat correlated as there can be similarities among their underlying algorithms

Many thanks !

Andy
